title: East Bengal Edge Past Indian Army 1-0 to Reach Durand Cup Semifinals
excerpt: Vishnu P.V. scores the only goal as East Bengal advance to face the winner of the Delhi-Raengdai quarterfinal, while Delhi thrash Raengdai 5-1 in the day's other knockout clash.
body:
• Vishnu P.V. scored in the 39th minute as East Bengal beat Indian Army FT 1-0 in the Durand Cup quarterfinal at Kolkata's Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan
  • Delhi demolished Raengdai 5-1 in the first quarterfinal at Ranchi, with Joseph scoring twice
  • East Bengal will face Delhi in the semifinal on August 19, while Mohun Bagan vs Jamshedpur and NorthEast United vs Shillong Lajong complete the last-eight stage on August 17
  • The 135th edition final is scheduled for August 23 at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan in Kolkata

East Bengal secured their place in the Durand Cup semifinals with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Indian Army Football Team in the second quarterfinal at Kolkata's Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on Saturday.

Vishnu P.V. — the tournament's standout attacker who struck a hat-trick in East Bengal's 8-0 group-stage demolition of CISF Protectors — scored the decisive goal in the 39th minute, continuing his prolific run in the 135th edition of Asia's oldest football tournament.

A Tight Quarterfinal in Kolkata

The match proved a far closer contest than East Bengal's group-stage routs might have suggested. Indian Army FT, who topped Group B to earn their knockout place, proved disciplined opponents and restricted East Bengal's attacking width for long stretches.

East Bengal's breakthrough came just before halftime when Vishnu found the net in the 39th minute, converting in front of 6,251 spectators. The Red and Gold Brigade held their lead through a tense second half, with Indian Army pressing for an equalizer that never materialized.

The victory means East Bengal, who qualified as the best runners-up from Group A behind arch-rivals Mohun Bagan, have now advanced to the semifinal stage where they will face Delhi on August 19 in Kolkata.

Delhi Cruise Past Raengdai

Earlier in the day at Ranchi's Birsa Munda Stadium, Delhi produced a dominant display to dispatch Raengdai 5-1 in the first quarterfinal, booking their semifinal berth in emphatic fashion.

Raengdai took an early lead through Kisan in the 9th minute, but Delhi responded with ruthless efficiency. Joseph scored twice in the 57th and 67th minutes to turn the match around, before Rodriguinho (81st minute), Juan Peña (90+3') and Augustine (90+7') completed the rout.

The 29,265-strong Ranchi crowd witnessed a comprehensive second-half performance from Delhi, who scored all five goals after the break.

Road to the Final

The remaining two quarterfinals take place on Sunday, August 17. Mohun Bagan — who beat East Bengal 1-0 in the group stage thanks to a Sahal Abdul Samad strike — face Jamshedpur at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, while NorthEast United meet Shillong Lajong at Shillong's Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.

The semifinals are scheduled for August 19 and 20, with the final set for August 23 in Kolkata. East Bengal will be hoping Vishnu's goal-scoring form can carry them all the way to the title in what has been a resurgent tournament campaign after their disappointing loss to Mohun Bagan in the group opener.
